title: Arithmetic and condensed resolution with rank zero for the zero ring
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E/Q_ell and O its recorded topological integer ring. For every continuous unital map a:O→A to a finite discrete commutative ring killed by an ell-power, there exist r, continuous O-linear maps phi:O^r→O^r and q:O^r→A with q surjective, phi injective, image phi=ker q and a matrix for phi. The continuous-section module of O^r is the finite biproduct of r regular condensed O-modules; if A is zero then r=0. Postcomposition by phi and q gives specified condensed arrows F,G with a zero composite, a short exact sequence and an identity-underlying identification of the quotient with restricted regular condensed A. No derived assertion is included.

source.place: Finite free and finitely presented coefficient extensions and Formal properties

proof.text: If A is nonzero, apply the already-proved finite_integral_condensed_resolution. If A is zero, take r=0 and zero maps. All algebraic exactness and the kernel homeomorphism follow by subsingleton elimination.

Coordinate projections and insertions on continuous functions give a bicone. Their composites are Kronecker identities, and their finite sum is identity sectionwise. The biproduct total-identity criterion supplies its finite-free isomorphism, including rank zero.

Apply continuousSections_finiteDiscrete_shortExact to the presentation and its kernel homeomorphism. Its section formulas are the required ones; identify the quotient with the restricted regular A-module by the identity.
